key_points.text: My guest this episode is Jeff Yan, founder of Chameleon Trading.
key_points.evidence_quote: My guest this episode is Jeff Yan, founder of Chameleon Trading.

key_points.text: Jeff began his career in high frequency trading at Hudson River.
key_points.evidence_quote: Jeff began his career in high frequency trading at Hudson River, but soon moved over to the world of crypto where he built one of the largest market-making firms in the space.

key_points.text: After Jeff gets me up to speed with the basics of high-frequency market making, we dive into some of the more esoteric components.
key_points.evidence_quote: After Jeff gets me up to speed with the basics of high-frequency market making, we dive into some of the more esoteric components, particularly with respect to centralized crypto exchanges.

key_points.text: These include infrastructure quirks, adversarial algorithms, and why HFTPNL might actually be predictive of medium-term price movements.
key_points.evidence_quote: These include infrastructure quirks, adversarial algorithms, and why HFTPNL might actually be predictive of medium-term price movements.

thesis: The guest explains that high-frequency market making is more infrastructure-heavy and latency-sensitive due to the need to avoid slow execution and large implicit exposure, whereas market taking is more statistics and model-heavy and allows for slower strategies that only need to perform well when they trigger. The guest notes that while both strategies are infrastructure-intensive, they represent opposite approaches where making requires constant readiness to avoid painful heavy tails, while taking offers the luxury of being smart only when a trade occurs.
